text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A group of World Bank directors is arriving in Moscow to inspect how the 1996 coal loan was used in the Russian mining regions of Rostov and Kemerovo. The future of the 1997 loan depends on results of this trip.
- Russia's First Deputy Primew Minister Anatoly Chubais is to discuss the 1998 federal budget and regional economic development today in the Siberian city of Krasnoyarsk.
- The European Bank of Reconstruction and Development is to expand its loan to gas giant Gazprom up to $300 million.
- Internal anarchy is a more important enemy for the Chechen authorities than the "imperial centre".
- Sberbank, Russia's state-controlled saving bank, is not planning to lower interest rates, fearing the outflow of the personal depositors' capital.
- Today's emergency government meeting on housing reform is a result of activity of Moscow mayor Yuri Luzhkov who demands special conditions for Russia's capital.
- The latest kidnapping of Russian journalists in Chechnya proves once again that situation is out of control in this postwar republic.
- Most of the paper's readers support unification of Russia and Belarus.
- Chechen kidnappers seized Russian journalists working for the NTV, the most popular TV company in the region, and they are likely to pay a high price for it.
